summary: The lexical relevance gate must match against the abstract as well as the title and topic, and must require TWO distinct claim stems rather than one — falling back to one stem only when the work carries no abstract, since the second could then only come from text the record does not have. Whatever it removes must be reported: the run emits fetched_count, relevance_excluded and pico_excluded alongside relevant_count, so the exclusion arithmetic closes as fetched = relevance + pico + relevant and relevant = retracted + scored. This SUPERSEDES the relevance-gate half of claim-aware-stance-polarity-and-claim-relevance-gate, whose summary still describes the single-token title/topic rule; the stance-polarity half of that entry is untouched and still applies.
reason: A single shared stem is satisfied by any paper mentioning one half of the claim, and the five-character truncation makes every token a prefix — so `vitamin` becomes `vitam`, which matches vitamin A, B, C, D and K alike. Measured on a live keyless run of 'vitamin C prevents the common cold': a vitamin K ferroptosis paper entered the score as REFUTING at 0.90 confidence, and a paper on cold-dependent anthocyanin accumulation in blood oranges entered as SUPPORTING at 0.90 — the second on the word 'cold' meaning a storage temperature. Six other repair directions were measured and rejected on collateral damage: narrowing the OpenAlex query, waking the PICO gate, adding topic metadata to the matched text, and three stricter token/stem settings, one of which emptied the vaccines corpus entirely. What survived is the only setting that removes the two off-topic works while moving none of the six calibrated harm corpora and keeping every apex-design work except a vitamin A review. The reporting half is not cosmetic and must not be dropped in a regen: the same change takes silent removal on that corpus from 1 work to 17, and a gate that quietly discards a third of the corpus is indistinguishable from a query that never found those works. Two properties are load-bearing and easy to lose: the stems must be counted DISTINCT (one stem found twice is one match), and the truncation length must stay a literal local to the relevance gate rather than the shared claimStemLen constant, which also drives the stance harm path and the PICO gate and is calibrated against the harm corpora.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test green across the module. Regression suite pinned to production over 13 archived corpora (295 studies): the harness reproduces relevantToClaim on 295 of 295. Control group unmoved, 0 of the 6 harm corpora. On the vitamin C corpus both off-topic works are excluded by DOI (10.1038/s41586-022-05022-3, 10.1105/tpc.111.095232) while all nine named apex works stay, including the Marine Recruits RCT (10.1001/jama.1979.03290350028016) that the title-only variants lost; 11 of 12 apex-design works survive, the exception being a vitamin A Cochrane meta-analysis (10.1002/14651858.cd008524.pub3) that only ever matched on `vitam`. Dissent is not removed faster than the corpus: works 295 to 261 (88.5% kept), refuting+mixed 67 to 64 (95.5% kept), +7.0 percentage points in dissent's favour. Exclusion reporting verified at 0, 1, 17 and 48 exclusions, on the real corpus (49 fetched, 32 kept, 17 excluded) and on the branch where nothing survives at all. Known limit recorded rather than fixed: because the haystack now includes the abstract, the two-stem bar is partly satisfiable by methodological boilerplate — measured with four off-topic claims over the 49-work corpus, three admitted nothing and one admitted a single work with a 24,724-character abstract, matching `quant`/`chrom`/`confi` on 'quantifying', 'chromatography' and 'confirmed'. The exposure scales with abstract length because the gate runs before clipAbstract.
